proposition_text: American cities would be more affordable today if they had legalized denser housing two decades earlier.
Advanced economies should legally redefine the standard full-time workweek to four days with no reduction in base pay for most full-time employees.
Countries should phase out tobacco sales through a generational ban rather than rely only on conventional age restrictions.
Museums and universities should return Indigenous and colonized peoples' human remains promptly even when researchers argue that continued scientific study would be valuable.
The U.S. national debt has reached a level where serious deficit reduction should take priority over most new spending commitments.
Anti-encampment laws are justified only when cities provide genuinely available shelter, storage, and service options rather than simply criminalize visible poverty.
Cities should impose congestion pricing in central districts even when drivers strongly oppose it.
Countries should reintroduce wolves, lynx, and other apex predators to restore degraded ecosystems even when rural communities and livestock farmers object.

Stablecoin issuers should be regulated more like banks or money-market funds than like ordinary software projects.
Most cryptocurrency trading platforms should be regulated as securities exchanges or broker-dealers rather than as a distinct lightly supervised asset category.
Bodily autonomy carries more moral weight than appeals to dignity in personal medical choices.
Cities should ban new single-family-only zoning districts entirely rather than just allow incremental density bonuses.
Retailers should be banned from using personalized algorithmic dynamic pricing based on a customer's perceived willingness or ability to pay.
Employers should stop using standardized personality tests such as MBTI and DISC in hiring and team-building because they have too little predictive validity.
Recreational genetic enhancement for aesthetic or non-medical physical traits in consenting adults should be strictly prohibited.
The U.S. strikes on Iranian military and nuclear targets were strategically justified despite the risk of a wider regional war.
AI is likely to eliminate more white-collar jobs than it creates, and policy should prepare early for that disruption.
Sanctuary cities are justified because they improve trust and public safety more than they undermine immigration enforcement.
Immigrants should be expected to adopt core civic norms and the common public language of the country they settle in, rather than treat cultural integration as optional.
College athletes at schools that directly share sports revenue should be represented through formal collective bargaining rather than ad hoc NIL and compliance systems.
Dating apps should make identity verification, block tools, and scam-response features free by default rather than reserve the best safety features for paying users.
Dating apps should limit engagement-maximizing swipe mechanics and paid visibility boosts when those features undermine match quality and user trust.
Dating apps should require stronger identity verification and fraud checks even if that makes sign-up slower and less anonymous.
Four-day school weeks harm student learning more than they help school districts save money and retain staff.
Cities should charge higher parking, registration, or curb fees for oversized SUVs and pickups when their size imposes higher safety and street-use costs.
Studios should need explicit performer consent and compensation before using AI de-aging or synthetic voice tools to materially alter a living actor's performance.
AI dubbing of actors' voices for film and television should require opt-in performer consent rather than rely on broad contract boilerplate.

Governments should ban social-media accounts for children under sixteen rather than rely mainly on parental controls and softer design changes.
Courts should be able to order temporary firearm removal through red-flag laws when credible evidence shows imminent risk even before a criminal conviction.
For carefully screened adolescents with persistent gender dysphoria, access to gender-affirming medical care improves mental-health outcomes more than it increases long-term regret or harm.

Public-school systems should provide universal free school meals without means testing rather than target support only to poorer students.
Restaurants should replace tipping-based compensation with higher base pay and clearly included service charges rather than rely on customer guilt and hidden labor costs.
Wealthy households should face an annual tax on large net worth rather than rely almost entirely on income and consumption taxes.
Young adults should be able to access mental-health treatment privately without parental notification or insurance billing that automatically reveals the visit.
Laws should allow competent adults with unbearable terminal or degenerative suffering to receive medical assistance in dying under strict safeguards.
Governments should subsidize rural broadband expansion even when private carriers argue that serving sparsely populated areas is not commercially viable.

Social media platforms should stop recommending political content by default unless users explicitly opt in to seeing it.
East Asian governments will raise birth rates more by improving housing affordability and childcare than by offering one-off cash bonuses for babies.
Parents should not use always-on location tracking and private-message monitoring of teenagers as a default household rule absent a specific safety concern.
Religious schools and employers should retain some room for faith-based dress expectations, but only when participation is genuinely voluntary and alternatives remain realistic.
Governments should legalize and regulate compensated surrogacy with strong protections against coercion and exploitation.
The eurozone's post-2010 crisis response deepened political distrust more than it preserved European solidarity.
Consumer brain-computer interfaces capable of writing to or stimulating the brain should be restricted to tightly regulated medical use rather than sold as ordinary consumer products.
Countries should globally prohibit the creation of novel synthetic viral pathogens with clear pandemic potential even for defensive-preparedness research.
High-burden malaria countries should permit tightly regulated outdoor gene-drive mosquito trials rather than block them until long-term ecological certainty is impossible.
Space agencies should shift most exploration budgets from crewed missions to robotic probes and telescopes that deliver more science per dollar.
Sovereign wealth funds are a better way for resource-rich developing countries to manage commodity windfalls than direct cash distributions to citizens.
Nuclear fusion research deserves continued large public investment even though commercially viable fusion power may still be decades away.
Countries should adopt an international treaty banning all kinetic anti-satellite weapons tests to prevent long-term orbital debris cascades.
Open-weight advanced AI models should remain legal by default unless they cross clearly specified capability and misuse thresholds that trigger stronger safeguards.
Courts should permit frozen sovereign assets from aggressor states to be used for reconstruction in the countries they harmed.
National-security review should presumptively block acquisitions of critical-mineral assets by firms closely tied to rival states.
Public pension systems should raise retirement ages in line with life expectancy rather than rely mainly on higher payroll taxes.
Governments should phase out universal fuel subsidies and replace them with targeted cash transfers rather than broad price controls.
The EU should implement asylum burden-sharing quotas rather than leave frontline states to manage most arrivals.
Countries should provide stronger compensation and archival access to survivors and descendants of forced-sterilization programs rather than treat those abuses as closed chapters.
Former state churches and religious orders should contribute financially to reparative funds when they played central roles in residential schools, forced assimilation, or similar historical abuses.

During recurring water shortages, cities and regions should use sharply rising prices for heavy users rather than rely mainly on blunt universal restrictions.

Automatic enrollment in retirement savings plans (with opt-out) would increase long-run household financial security more effectively than increasing tax deductions for voluntary retirement contributions.
For reducing traffic fatalities, automated speed enforcement delivers larger safety gains with fewer negative externalities than increasing traditional police traffic stops.
Nuclear power life-extension and new-build programs will reduce emissions faster per public dollar than an equivalent scale-up of wind, solar, and batteries in the 2026–2036 period.
Gulf and North African states should phase out universal fuel subsidies within five years and replace them with targeted cash transfers.
European and Latin American cities should permit regulated supervised consumption sites to reduce overdose deaths and public disorder.
European countries should expand preventive policing powers (such as wider stop-and-search) to curb knife and gang violence.
Large employers should be required to disclose pay bands and promotion rates by role, even if it reduces managerial flexibility.
Schools should treat student use of generative AI for assignments as permissible by default, requiring citation and process transparency rather than broad bans.
Consent alone is not enough to make a transaction ethical.
Democratic legitimacy matters more than technocratic competence in public decision-making.
Adult children should have a legally enforceable duty to contribute to the care costs of aging parents who cannot support themselves.
Governments should heavily restrict unpaid internships outside genuinely educational placements.
Governments should treat national well-being rather than GDP growth as the primary headline target for economic policy.
Countries should abolish seasonal clock changes and adopt permanent standard time rather than keep daylight saving time or move to permanent summer time.
Browsers and operating systems should be required by law to offer robust, opt-out ad and tracker blocking at the system level for all users.

Vacation-rental platforms should be required to show cleaning fees, resort fees, and house rules before users click into checkout or request to book.

A two-state solution between Israelis and Palestinians remains the least-bad achievable long-term outcome despite repeated failures and declining trust.
Wedding culture has become so expensive and performative that couples should feel little obligation to follow traditional expectations.
Algorithmic pricing that charges different customers different prices for effectively the same product should usually be disclosed or banned.
Space tourism is ethically hard to justify while climate change and severe global poverty remain unresolved priorities.
Public agencies should never suspend benefits, visas, or fraud claims solely because an AI risk model flags a person as suspicious without meaningful human review.
Parents should be allowed to impose operating-system-level age and recommendation limits on teenagers' devices that third-party apps cannot easily bypass.

Public statues and monuments honoring leaders primarily associated with slavery, colonial domination, or mass repression should be removed from places of civic honor and relocated to museums or contextualized sites.

Public schools should use history textbooks written under stronger independent scholarly review rather than leave narratives of war, colonialism, and national identity mainly to shifting political control.

Former colonial powers should fund conservation, provenance research, and museum capacity in countries receiving returned artifacts rather than treat restitution as complete once objects are shipped back.
Governments should rename public holidays, schools, and streets that primarily honor colonizers, slaveholders, or dictators rather than keep them in the name of historical continuity.

Governments should digitize and publicly fund access to family records linked to slavery, adoption, indigenous dispossession, and wartime displacement rather than leave historical recovery mostly to private genealogy markets.
Modern meritocracy is overstated, and elite educational and professional pathways still reproduce class privilege more than most successful people admit.
Professional sports leagues should keep a meaningful share of marquee games on free-to-air television rather than move them mostly behind subscription streaming paywalls.

AI companion apps marketed to lonely adults should face duty-of-care and emotional-manipulation rules rather than be treated as ordinary entertainment products.
Payment processors and app stores should not deny lawful adult-content creators access solely because platforms fear reputational risk.
Loot boxes and similar randomized in-game purchases should be regulated as gambling when sold to minors.
Public broadcasters should prioritize youth-oriented short-form video and creator partnerships rather than traditional channel expansion to remain relevant.
AI companion apps for minors should be regulated more like high-risk social products than like ordinary chatbots.

Obesity policy should focus more on food environment and marketing restrictions than on individual consumer behavior campaigns.
Insurers should not be allowed to price personal car insurance using continuous in-car behavior surveillance unless drivers opt in on genuinely fair terms.
Cities should use lower default urban speed limits and street redesign more than harsher post-crash penalties if the goal is to reduce traffic deaths.
Ride-hail services should be required to show drivers and riders the full fare split by default rather than keep pricing logic largely opaque.
Film studios should spend more on mid-budget original movies even if franchise sequels remain more predictable box-office bets.
Streaming bundles should be easier to pause, split, or reconfigure monthly rather than mimic the lock-in and opacity of old cable packages.
Teacher self-censorship caused by political pressure on curriculum is now a more serious threat to education quality than the controversial content that pressure is meant to police.
Credit card interest rates should be capped by law even if lenders respond by cutting credit access for higher-risk borrowers.
Large inheritances should be taxed much more aggressively because dynastic wealth is a bigger threat to equality of opportunity than most high earners' annual income.
Governments should legalize and regulate cultivated meat on the same basic terms as conventional meat once safety standards are met.
Cities and countries should phase out the most wasteful single-use takeaway packaging even if consumers and small businesses face some inconvenience and transition costs.

Governments should use subsidized prediction markets as a formal input to major policy decisions rather than rely mainly on expert panels and internal forecasts.
Governments should expand universal basic services such as transit, internet, childcare, and healthcare rather than spend the same money on unconditional cash transfers.
Small island developing states should be granted weighted voting power in international climate negotiations proportional to their existential risk rather than their population or GDP.

The dominance of English as the global language of science, business, and the internet does more harm than good to non-anglophone cultures and knowledge systems.

WHO members should give the organization stronger outbreak-verification access even if it constrains national control over early crisis messaging.
